title: Frog in the Pan: Continuous Information and Momentum
one_line: Momentum is much stronger in stocks whose past return came from many small moves ('continuous information') than from a few big jumps; investors under-react to information that arrives gradually.

findings.statement: Continuous-information winners/losers drive momentum; discrete-information momentum is weak.

why.pattern: Limited attention to small, frequent changes.

reported_results.headline: Momentum is much stronger in stocks whose past return came from many small moves ('continuous information') than from a few big jumps; investors under-react to information that arrives gradually.

tradable_edge: Stock-level. A single-asset analogue (trend built from many small days vs a few big days) could be a filter on trend_risk_timing_overlay_es — note only.
data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
caveats: Only the abstract / a secondary summary was reachable (SSRN is blocked from chat sessions); numbers not verified against the full paper.
